deep.reconstruction:
Context: the notes on systems of pseudo-lines (arrangements of pseudo-lines, a topological and combinatorial subject; the previous page counts cells of an arrangement) need a topological Stein factorization. Grothendieck works in topological spaces over a base X, crossing out what is probably 'de Top_{/X}'.

(1) Setup. Let f: Z -> X be continuous. Its Stein factorization is Z -> Z~ -> X. Here Z~ is the set of connected components of the fibres Z_x, with the quotient topology, so Z -> Z~ has connected fibres. Call a map Z' -> X' 'steinien' if it is surjective with connected fibres and X' carries the quotient topology. In the notes Z' ≃ X' means exactly this: Z' is X' up to connected fibres.

(2) Universal property. Suppose given a square Z <- Z', X <- X' with Z' -> X' steinien. Each fibre Z'_{x'} is connected and maps into Z_{x}, x the image of x', so it lands in one connected component of Z_x. This defines a set map X' -> Z~. It is continuous because X' has the quotient topology from Z'. It is unique because Z' -> X' is surjective. It is an X-morphism and makes the square Z <- Z', Z~ <- X' commute.

Reformulation: in the category of steinien maps Z' -> X' lying over Z -> X, the object (Z -> Z~) is universal. Grothendieck calls it 'initial'. With morphisms taken as squares mapping toward (Z -> X) it is rather terminal; this is a convention issue.

(3) Base change. Take a cartesian square Z' = Z x_X X'. Question: when is the induced lower square Z~' -> Z~ over X' -> X also cartesian? Equivalently, when does Stein factorization commute with base change? Two candidate sufficient conditions are listed:
(a) Z -> X compact, i.e. proper. This is the topological proper base change for pi_0 / H^0 of fibres.
(b) X' -> X locally 0-acyclic (or locally G-acyclic). This is the analogue of smooth / locally acyclic base change.
These parallel the algebro-geometric facts: Stein factorization (EGA III 4.3) commutes with flat base change via f_*O_Z, and the proper / smooth base change theorems of SGA 4.
errors: Calling (Z -> Z~) an 'initial' object is a matter of orientation. Since the canonical maps go from the other objects to it (X' -> Z~), it is terminal under the natural orientation.
The universal property needs 'steinien' to include surjectivity and quotient topology on X'. Connected fibres alone do not give continuity or uniqueness of X' -> Z~. This is implicit and not stated.
In the topological setting Z~ need not be well behaved (e.g. Hausdorff) unless Z -> X is proper. The base-change question is left open with only the two candidate hypotheses listed.

ideas.what: Universal property of the topological Stein factorization Z -> Z~ -> X (space of connected components of fibres)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stein (complex analytic), Grothendieck EGA III (schemes); Whyburn / Eilenberg monotone-light factorization in topology

ideas.what: Compatibility of Stein factorization with base change under properness or local acyclicity of the base change
ideas.modern_name: proper base change / locally acyclic (smooth) base change for H^0 / pi_0
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 XII, XV, XVI (étale analogues); EGA III

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard auxiliary material: a topological Stein factorization and its base-change behaviour, written as a working tool for the pseudo-line study. The only interest is seeing Grothendieck carry his SGA 4 base-change reflexes into elementary topology around 1981. Nothing new mathematically.
